title: Marathon Myths Debunked by NYRR Staffers (2026-11-07 recheck: a direct request returns 404 from this network; the full text was retrieved through an external fetch channel and all six recorded claims matched word for word)
claims: The article was published on 17 October 2019.
An NYRR coach states that the highest point of the race is in the first two miles, at about 260 ft above sea level.
The same article states that the Verrazzano Bridge is the highest hill on the course, in miles 1 and 2.
The article places the Queensboro Bridge at miles 15 to 16 and Fifth Avenue at miles 22 to 23.
The article states that the marathon enters the Bronx during mile 20 and exits it just after mile 21.

The article describes three start lines and refers to a green wave taking the lower level of the Verrazzano Bridge, wording that differs from the 2026 race and start pages' blue, orange and pink colours.

claimVerification.note: Myth: really hilly 段，教练 Ben Delaney：“The highest point of the race is in the first two miles, at a whopping 260 ft above sea level”。
同段：“The highest hill in the TCS New York City Marathon is the Verrazzano Bridge. That is, miles 1 and 2.”
同段：“You have the Queensboro Bridge at miles 15 to 16 and then Fifth Avenue at miles 22 to 23.”
Bronx myth 段：“The marathon enters the Bronx during mile 20 and exits it just after mile 21.”
Green wave myth 段：“The New York City Marathon has three separate start lines… The blue and orange waves begin atop the Verrazzano Bridge. The green wave takes off on the bridge’s lower level.”
